analysis: The code calls `substring(beginIndex)` where `beginIndex = pos + 1`, with `pos = path.lastIndexOf('.')`. Before the call, there is a check `if (pos >= 0)`, which ensures that a dot exists. This guarantees `beginIndex >= 1`. Since `pos` is the index of the last dot, the maximum possible `pos` is `path.length() - 1` (when the string ends with a dot), so `beginIndex <= path.length()`. Therefore, `beginIndex` is always non-negative and not greater than the string length, avoiding `IndexOutOfBoundsException`. The only declared exception is `IndexOutOfBoundsException`, and its condition is fully avoided by the guard.
remark: No exceptions are triggered because the guard `pos >= 0` ensures the substring index is always within valid bounds (1 to length inclusive). An empty string with no dot bypasses the call entirely. Thus, all throwing conditions are avoided.
